newsitem.title: USA: US rep urging Congress to relax curbs on IDBs-aide.
newsitem.headline: US rep urging Congress to relax curbs on IDBs-aide.

text.p: U.S. Rep Phil English, R-Pa., a member of the powerful House Ways and Means Committee, said he will reintroduce a bill to relax curbs on small-issue industrial development bonds (IDBs) when the 105th Congress convenes tomorrow.
Congress wiped out commercial IDBs in the Tax Reform Act of 1986 and called for elimination of manufacturing IDBs by December 31, 1989.

But recognizing the amount of job-creation that resulted from IDBs, Congress temporarily extended the manufacturing IDB exemption several times before making it permanent, English said in a press statement this week.
English first offered legislation in 1994, but neither the House nor Senate voted on the measure.
The bill would hike from $10 million to $20 million the capital expenditure limit for IDBs, English said.

It also would increase the volume cap from $50 per capita to $75 to cover inflation, he said. And it would clearly define the term "core manufacturing" to give agencies a better idea about what projects qualify for IDB financing, he said.
"IDBs have served a strategic role in local economic development efforts," English said. "My legislation ... will make IDBs even more accessible as a tool for local job creation," he said.

IDBs are tax-exempt bonds issued by a public agency to finance certain types of facilities for private enterprises, including water and air pollution control, ports, airports, resource-recovery plants and housing. Most IDBs are issued by authorities set up by state and local governments.
